text: Pregnant sows: increase feed by 500 g/day during the first 3 weeks of pregnancy (to support placenta development) and again by 500 g/day during the last 3 weeks (rapid fetal growth); the diet should support some fat reserve buildup, since the sow will draw on these reserves for milk production during lactation. Lactating sows: need more energy and protein for milk production; feed at least 3 times a day to encourage intake. Feed quantity rises from about 1 kg on the first day after farrowing to a peak after about 1 week; total daily amount depends on litter size — for example a sow nursing 6 piglets needs about 5 kg/day, while one nursing 10 piglets needs at least 6.5 kg/day. Boars: often fed a diet similar to pregnant sows, with regular supplementary feed containing vitamins and amino acids to support sperm production.
